  "chapter": "education/027",
  "summary": "The revision is a competent, well-chosen compression. It keeps all eight protected passages, the key chronology (1893, 1895, 1900, 310, Cherbourg 19 Jan 1901), Langley's identification, the 'attitude not assertion' framing of Langley's disowning of the rays, and the Lucretius/Dante attribution. No must_fix problems were found. The cuts leave a few small residues, mostly where an antecedent or comparand was cut but its anaphor survived: the Boston chemist's logic, the 'all' and 'easiest' in the Virgin-versus-force passage, and the goddess-as-taste antithesis before the Chartres epigram. Other losses are defensible trade-offs, chiefly deflating wit and some connective tissue.",
  "verdict": "editorial_review",
  "coverage": [
    {
      "axis": "causality_and_setup",
      "status": "findings",
      "assessment": "The main arc survives (Exposition, dynamo, rupture, broken neck, rays into faith, Virgin as force, scholastic pursuit, sailing). Residues: the chemist's logic is cut loose from its setup; the 'all' and 'easiest' in the closing Virgin passage lose their comparand; the 'literary knowledge' of para 1 loses its antecedent; the 'faith' plant in the dynamo passage is gone."
    },
    {
      "axis": "referents_and_scene",
      "status": "findings",
      "assessment": "Langley is identified at first mention and his pronouns stay clear. The Amiens scene is intact (portal, Gibbon, Ruskin, St. Gaudens). Minor referent thinning: 'literary knowledge' without the Bacon work named, 'this energy' with the Virgin unnamed in para 12, and 'all' in para 18."
    },
    {
      "axis": "dialogue",
      "status": "no_material_issue",
      "assessment": "There is no dialogue in the chapter. The only quotations are Gibbon's phrase (attributed correctly and verbatim) and the Lucretius line."
    },
    {
      "axis": "qualification_and_facts",
      "status": "findings",
      "assessment": "The hedges are mostly preserved: 'perhaps himself' for Gibbon, 'perhaps at Lourdes', 'would risk translating rays into faith', and Langley's anarchical/parricidal attitude. Radium 'denied its God' stays framed as Langley's view ('what was to Langley the same thing'). The one real loss is the dangling quantifier 'all were occult' once radium is cut."
    },
    {
      "axis": "viewpoint_and_revelation",
      "status": "no_material_issue",
      "assessment": "The retrospective third-person distance holds. The 1895 and 1893 dates are kept distinct, and no later knowledge is imported."
    },
    {
      "axis": "voice_and_rhythm",
      "status": "findings",
      "assessment": "The semicolon series and epigram endings are kept (V1–V8). Some deflating asides are lost, notably 'Since no one else showed much concern…', the fig-leaf/magazine-female wit, the Milky Way contrast, and the 'cared nothing for the sex of the dynamo' line. The prose is tauter and slightly less comic, which is acceptable at this length."
    },
    {
      "axis": "interpretive_structure",
      "status": "findings",
      "assessment": "The Virgin-as-force thesis is intact. The steam/Virgin contrast is weakened because two supports were cut: the sentence that artists felt goddesses only as taste, and the explicit comparison of the Virgin's attraction with 'all the steam-engines and dynamos'. The Virgin-to-Dynamo pivot sentence is also gone."
    },
    {
      "axis": "planned_dependencies",
      "status": "findings",
      "assessment": "Four of the five dependencies are intact at both endpoints. The Chicago endpoint is intact locally, but its partner chapter has no published draft. The 310 benchmark survives locally; the partner's 'Civitas Dei' elaboration was cut in the existing production draft, leaving only a bare '310'."
    }
  ],

      "id": "F1",
      "priority": "should_improve",
      "axis": "causality_and_setup",
      "title": "Boston chemist's point loses its logical setup and its second term",
      "origin": "first_draft_worsened_by_revision",
      "claim": "The source sets up the chemist as the sceptic of a 'reversible process' who 'could not deny' he could feel the force of both rays and Virgin. It also lists his ignorance of dynamos, automobiles and radium alongside Venus and the Virgin. The revision cuts the sceptic frame and the dynamos/radium clause, so 'the force of all' now has only Venus and the Virgin as antecedents. 'The rays were unborn' then has no matching ignorance of the rays.",
      "reader_effect": "The chemist is a sudden aside whose purpose (the mind can feel both kinds of force, which justifies translating rays into faith) is no longer stated.",
      "evidence": [
        {"document": "education/027/source", "paragraph": 8, "quote": "Such a reversible process would vastly amuse a chemist, but the chemist could not deny that he, or some of his fellow physicists, could feel the force of both."},
        {"document": "education/027/source", "paragraph": 8, "quote": "neither had he heard of dynamos or automobiles or radium; yet his mind was ready to feel the force of all"},
        {"document": "education/027/revision", "paragraph": 8, "quote": "yet his mind was ready to feel the force of all, though the rays were unborn and the women were dead."}
      ],
      "counterevidence": "The plan only asks for the chemist who never heard of Venus or the Virgin, yet could feel such forces, and that much survives. 'Rays' and 'faith' sit one sentence earlier, so a reader can partly infer the point.",
      "plan_relation": "Required (chemist kept); the connective logic is a planning gap.",
      "minimal_repair": "Restore a short clause such as 'neither had he heard of dynamos or radium; yet his mind could feel the force of both'.",
      "confidence": "medium"
    },

      "axis": "interpretive_structure",
      "title": "Antithesis behind the Chartres epigram is thinned",
      "origin": "first_draft",
      "claim": "In the source, the 'railway train as power' sentence answers a statement that neither St. Gaudens nor Arnold felt goddesses as power, only as emotion, beauty and taste. Only the pivot 'but otherwise one must look for force to the goddesses of Indian mythology' remains, so the contrast the epigram resolves is implicit.",
      "reader_effect": "V8 still lands as an epigram, but the force/taste opposition that links it to V7 is left to inference.",
      "evidence": [
        {"document": "education/027/source", "paragraph": 20, "quote": "Neither of them felt goddesses as power--only as reflected emotion, human expression, beauty, purity, taste"},
        {"document": "education/027/revision", "paragraph": 17, "quote": "Artists felt a railway train as power, yet they constantly complained that the power embodied in a railway train could never be embodied in art."}
      ],
      "counterevidence": "V7 (force versus taste) sits just above and carries the contrast; the Arnold comparison was authorised for cutting.",
      "plan_relation": "Optional tradeoff for Arnold; the missing 'taste' sentence is a small planning omission.",
      "minimal_repair": "Insert a short clause before the railway sentence, e.g. 'They felt goddesses only as taste or emotion, never as power; they felt a railway train as power…'.",

      "claim": "The source states that the Virgin could scarcely be more complex than radium, then says Adams knew nothing about 'any of them'.       "reader_effect": "The closing judgment that the Virgin is 'easiest to handle' has nothing explicit to be easier than, and 'all' dangles.",
